name: Bolt Business
summary: Business travel and mobility management. Give your team expense-tracked rides and travel with centralized billing and reporting.
best_for: companies with European/African travel footprints that want employee rides centrally billed, policy-controlled and expense-integrated — at zero platform cost
skip_if: you operate in the US only (network coverage), or you need guaranteed fixed-price corporate transport contracts
honest_knock: The honest boundary is geography: Bolt's network is Europe/Africa-centric across 600+ cities, so US-only operations should look elsewhere, and ride availability varies by city — pilot it on your team's actual routes. Pricing is dynamic like all ride-hailing; the business layer adds control and receipts, not fixed corporate fares, so budget-predictability comes from your spend limits, not from locked prices.

pricing.notes: No subscription, no activation cost and no minimum commitment (re-verified 2026-08-20 on Bolt's own business page): you pay per ride or rental taken, with consolidated monthly billing, spend limits and policy controls included. One line the marketing does not carry, but Bolt's own support pages do: Bolt charges a service fee on every trip made with the business payment method, billed at the start of the following month. On credit card it is deducted automatically and does not appear on the individual trip invoice — it arrives as a separate service fee statement on the 3rd of each month; on postpaid it sits on the monthly invoice. The amount is not published. Still commitment-free to pilot, but ‘you only pay for the rides’ is not the whole bill.

compare_with.name: Uber for Business
compare_with.why: the direct rival — Uber wins on US/global coverage, Bolt typically on per-ride cost in its home markets; run both where they overlap
